title: Compositional Generalisation for Explainable Hate Speech Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating compositional generalisation using the TARGET benchmark, which features unseen combinations of targets and expressions, and applying the AAA (Adversarial Attacks against Abuse) metric to measure and penalise a model's reliance on shallow lexical features and training set correlations.

Testing models on synthetic hate speech data to ensure they do not rely on biased stereotypical associations, such as exclusively associating derogatory comparisons like 'terrorists' with the Muslim community.

Evaluating models on the TARGET benchmark, which introduces novel combinations of national groups (e.g., immigrants, Taiwanese, Mongolians, Ukrainians, Colombians) and derogatory expressions to measure fair generalisation across different nationalities.

Measuring hate speech detection performance on synthetic datasets (U-PLEAD and TARGET) that deliberately balance the frequencies of specific racial and ethnic groups (e.g., Pacific Islanders, Arab Americans) across all classes to decouple them from stereotypical hateful expressions.

Assessing model generalisation on synthetic datasets that systematically balance gender-related protected targets (e.g., 'women', 'pregnancy') across both hateful and non-hateful contexts to prevent learned demographic biases.
